stemMd: A university plans to offer a night class because a survey found that many daytime students work during the evening. The dean concludes that those students will find the night class easier to attend. Which information reveals the central mistaken assumption?

options.label: B
options.textMd: Some students have never taken a night class.

options.label: C
options.textMd: Night classes can have smaller enrolments.

options.label: D
options.textMd: Students differ in their preferred subjects.

options.label: E
options.textMd: The reasoning assumes that evening work does not prevent attendance at an evening class.

explanationMd: Focus on the claimed benefit for the surveyed students. Evening employment is evidence of an obstacle to evening attendance, not evidence of availability. The argument has treated the conflicting time commitment as though it favored the proposed schedule.

distractorRationale.b: Past experience is not required for attendance.
distractorRationale.c: Class size does not remove the work conflict.
distractorRationale.a: Room ownership does not establish students' availability.
distractorRationale.d: Subject preference is not the scheduling conflict described.
